See also: theatre and théatre

French

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

    Borrowed from Latin theātrum, from Ancient Greek θέατρον (théatron, “a place for viewing”), from θεάομαι (theáomai, “to see, to watch, to observe”).

    Pronunciation

    [edit]
    • (Paris) IPA(key): /te.ɑtʁ/
      • Audio; “le théâtre”:(file)
    • (Switzerland, Belgium) IPA(key): [teˈaːtʁ̥]
      • Audio (Brussels):(file)
    • (Switzerland, Canton of Valais; Quebec, standard) IPA(key): [te.ˈɑːtʁ̥]
      • Audio (Switzerland (Valais)):(file)
    • (Quebec, nonstandard) IPA(key): [teˈɑu̯tʁ̥]
      • Audio (Montreal):(file)
    • Audio (France (Saint-Maurice-de-Beynost)):(file)
    • Audio (France (Toulouse)):(file)
    • Audio (France (Vosges)):(file)
    • Audio (France (Lyon)):(file)

    Noun

    [edit]

    théâtre m (plural théâtres)

    1. theatre (venue for performing plays and drama; performing art form)
    2. (Missouri, Louisiana) a movie theater

    Derived terms

    [edit]
    • amphithéâtre
    • coup de théâtre
    • pièce de théâtre
    • théâtral
